tagline: Through canyons and forests on parts of three historic trails
intro: The Morgan–Parleys drive winds through canyons, farmland and forests, passing East Canyon State Park between Morgan and I-80. Visit Utah gives the trip as 33 miles and 50 minutes and highlights its connections with the Mormon, California and Pony Express trails. Utah designated the corridor a state scenic byway on December 11, 2017.

The road’s relationship to the Mormon Trail was deliberate: when SR 65 joined the state highway system in 1931, it followed that trail as closely as practicable over Big Mountain Pass and through Emigration Canyon to Salt Lake City. SR 66 itself had begun in 1931 as the state connection from Hardscrabble through Porterville to Morgan. The Hardscrabble link left state control in 1953, before the later southward extension brought East Canyon Reservoir into the numbered route. In 1969, the state rerouted SR 65 to I-80 in Parleys Canyon and extended SR 66 from Porterville to East Canyon Reservoir.

From Morgan, SR 66 follows East Canyon Creek through East Canyon, then winds along the reservoir’s northern end. At SR 65, turn south for Big Mountain Pass, the 7,420-foot crossing used by Mormon pioneers in 1847. The road then passes Little Dell Reservoir before reaching I-80 near Mountain Dell Dam.

moments.title: Morgan
moments.text: Commercial Street became Morgan’s business center when merchants moved closer to the railroad’s freight and passenger stations. Union Pacific laid tracks through Weber Canyon in 1868–1869. Businesses shifted to the west side of the tracks, and Commercial Street remains the town’s main street and the focus of its historic district. The depot at 98 North Commercial Street dates to 1926 and served passengers until 1972. Ownership passed from Union Pacific to Morgan County in 1982. A steel caboose displayed near the depot once served as a crew shuttle in Ogden before its donation to Morgan in 2019.

moments.title: East Canyon State Park
moments.text: A 680-acre reservoir occupies the narrow-walled canyon at East Canyon State Park. East Canyon Creek feeds the water held behind a concrete arch dam built between 1964 and 1966. The dam stands 259 feet high and stretches 436 feet across, with a base 20 feet wide and a crest only 7 feet wide. SR 66 winds along the northern end of the reservoir before meeting SR 65. The reservoir belongs to the Weber Basin Project. The park sits at 5,700 feet above sea level, below the byway’s crossing at Big Mountain Pass.

moments.title: Big Mountain Pass
moments.text: Big Mountain Pass carries the road over a 7,420-foot crossing in the Wasatch Mountains. The Donner Party used it in 1846, followed in 1847 by Mormon pioneers heading for the Salt Lake Valley. When the state established SR 65 in 1931, it kept as close as practicable to the historic Mormon Trail over this pass. Snowfall determines the seasonal closure at the crossing.

practical: Big Mountain Pass: SR 65 south of Big Mountain to Little Dell Reservoir closes for approximately six months each winter and spring. (checked 2026-10-11)
